title.value: Implicit Offline Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning
title.justification: The title effectively encapsulates the core focus of the study, which is the development and testing of an implicit offline reinforcement learning framework using supervised learning methodologies.
title.quote: I MPLICIT O FFLINE R EINFORCEMENT L EARNING VIA S UPERVISED L EARNING

extractions.description: This paper presents a new method, Implicit Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning (IRvS), which leverages implicit models to learn robotic skills from offline datasets of varying levels of expertise. The approach contrasts with traditional explicit models by using a single unified framework without needing to discretize variables or specify target returns explicitly. The method demonstrates superior performance in high-dimensional tasks such as ADROIT manipulation and FrankaKitchen tasks when compared to both explicit and other state-of-the-art methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The core theme of this paper is not directed towards climate or ecological sustainable development. Instead, it focuses on developing a new reinforcement learning technique for robotic tasks, which is more generally applicable to various machine learning tasks.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) via Supervised Learning is a simple and effective way to learn robotic skills from a dataset

primary_category.justification: There are no direct implications or applications discussed in the paper related to climate change or ecological sustainable development. The primary focus is on reinforcement learning methodologies and artificial intelligence frameworks.
primary_category.quote: Despite the benefits of using implicit models to learn robotic skills via BC, offline RL via Supervised Learning algorithms have been limited to explicit models.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories related to climate change or ecological impact do not apply as the paper primarily addresses machine learning techniques without explicit sustainable development concerns.
primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we bridge the gap between implicit models and RvS, and propose the first implicit RvS algorithm.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not need a new category within sustainable development because it focuses on advancing AI techniques, not specific to sustainability initiatives.
new_primary_category.quote: A practical and straightforward approach to leveraging large and varied robotics datasets is to convert the RL problem into a supervised learning problem.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new sub-category as the paper is within the domain of AI and ML advancements, unrelated to climate or ecology.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We propose instead to model the state conditional distribution over returns p(G | s) using supervised learning by discretizing the returns.
